headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty fell sharply as IT stocks faced selling pressure and profit booking

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 30 November.

why: Heavy selling pressure in IT stocks dragged the benchmark indices lower during the last session.
Profit booking by investors after recent gains pulled the Sensex and Nifty down.
Lingering risks of US Fed rate hikes created caution across global and domestic markets.
Broad-based market weakness outweighed strength in metal and defence stocks.
whatHappening: In the last session, Sensex and Nifty closed in the red with IT leading the overall market decline.
Gold rebounded from 15-month lows while silver prices surged nearly 6%.
Bombay High Court gave permission for the Tata Sons board meeting scheduled for November 30.
OPEC+ is expected to keep oil production targets steady while copper rose on China support.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian equity markets closed lower as IT stocks led a broad sell-off driven by profit booking. Metal and defence stocks showed resilience, while precious metals like gold and silver saw strong rebounds. The market is closed today for the weekend and will resume trading on Monday, 30 November.
